facts.fact_text: On 18 May 2007 the applicant was travelling to Samara to take part in the opposition rally called 'March of Dissent'.
The opposition rally 'March of Dissent' had been organised to coincide with the EU-Russia summit scheduled for 17 and 18 May 2007 in Samara.
The applicant was accompanied by several activists who were also travelling to the 'March of Dissent' rally in Samara on 18 May 2007.
The applicant submits that, when he presented his passport for identity check, police officer A. seized the applicant's passport.
The applicant submits that, when he presented his passport for identity check, police officer A. seized the applicant's ticket.
The applicant submits that he was required to leave the check-in area and to follow police officer A.
The applicant submits that he was taken to a police office on the second floor of Sheremetyevo airport.
The applicant submits that five other persons from his group were escorted from the check-in hall in the same manner as the applicant.
At 11.20 a.m. on 18 May 2007, the applicant and the five others from his group were ordered to remain on the second floor of Sheremetyevo airport.
At 11.20 a.m. on 18 May 2007, the applicant and the five others from his group were informed that they would have to be questioned as to how they had purchased their allegedly forged tickets.
The applicant maintains that he was under orders not to leave the police office at Sheremetyevo airport.
The applicant maintains that he was prevented from leaving the police office at Sheremetyevo airport by an armed policeman who was guarding the doorway.
The applicant remained at the police station at Sheremetyevo airport until 1.30 p.m. on 18 May 2007.

The record (протокол) of search and confiscation completed by Captain N. records that the applicant's aeroplane ticket was confiscated in accordance with Articles 21.1, 27.7 and 27.10 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

Article 27.7 of the Code of Administrative Offences allows personal searches and searches of luggage carried by a person to be conducted if it is necessary to find an object or an instrument of an administrative offence.
Article 27.7 of the Code of Administrative Offences defines the search procedure and sets out the requirements of the search report.

Article 27.10 of the Code of Administrative Offences states that objects and instruments of an administrative offence, as well as documents that may serve as evidence in proceedings concerning an administrative offence, may be seized in accordance with the specified procedure.
The Government submitted that on 17 May 2007, the Department of the Interior's Sheremetyevo airport branch received information on forged tickets being sold for the 18 May 2007 Moscow-Samara flight.

The Government submitted that on 18 May 2007, officers from the Department of the Interior's Sheremetyevo airport branch, acting on information about forged tickets, were present at check-in and examined the tickets of all passengers on the Moscow-Samara flight.
The Government submitted that in the course of the ticket checks on 18 May 2007, twenty tickets bearing signs of forgery were found, having worn spots and dubious printing forms.
The Government submitted that the twenty tickets bearing signs of forgery were confiscated and the passengers who had presented them were prevented from boarding the Moscow-Samara flight.
The Government submitted that the confiscated tickets were subsequently sent for forensic examination.
The Government submitted that the forensic examination of the confiscated tickets showed thirteen tickets with signs of writing on top of the original text.

The Government commented that under section 11 of the Police Act (no. 1026-1 of 18 April 1991), the police had the right to seek an explanation from the applicant regarding the ticket, and he had been invited to provide one.
At 11.20 a.m. on 18 May 2007, the applicant and the five others from his group were ordered to remain on the second floor of Sheremetyevo airport.
At 11.20 a.m. on 18 May 2007, the applicant and the five others from his group were informed that they would have to be questioned as to how they had purchased their allegedly forged tickets.
The applicant remained at the police station at Sheremetyevo airport until 1.30 p.m. on 18 May 2007.
On the pro forma statement (объяснение), the applicant has written that from 8.30 a.m. until 12.50 p.m. on 18 May 2007 he had been deprived of his freedom of movement.
On the pro forma statement (объяснение), the applicant has written that no documents had been provided to him until 12.50 p.m. on 18 May 2007.
The handwritten declaration states that the applicant and five others were at the airport building under the surveillance of police officers, with their passports confiscated.

The handwritten declaration states that at 11.20 a.m. on 18 May 2007, police officers A., C. and S. categorically prohibited the applicant and five others from leaving the second floor of Sheremetyevo airport.

The handwritten declaration states that police officers A., C. and S. indicated that the applicant and five others had to provide an explanation to the police officers because some tickets were allegedly forged.

The handwritten declaration states that as of 12.20 p.m. on 18 May 2007, the applicant and five others were still detained in the hall of Sheremetyevo airport without any documents being provided to them.

The Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow found that there had been no grounds for applying the three-hour time-limit for the application of preventative measures in administrative offences cases as provided for by the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow found that there had been no grounds for the drawing up of a detention report (протокол о задержании).
The applicant complained to the Moscow Transport Prosecutor's Office about having been unlawfully detained by the police.
The applicant requested that the Moscow Transport Prosecutor's Office prosecute those responsible for his alleged unlawful detention.
On 28 June 2007, the prosecutor's office decided not to open criminal proceedings against the policemen involved in the events of 18 May 2007 at Sheremetyevo airport.

The prosecutor's office decision of 28 June 2007 stated that on 18 May 2007 the police, together with the Sheremetyevo airport security service, carried out a check of the passengers leaving on flight no. 813, Moscow–Samara.
The prosecutor's office decision of 28 June 2007 stated that during the check, thirteen plane tickets with traces of forgery were discovered and seized.
The prosecutor's office decision of 28 June 2007 stated that the police subsequently conducted an inquiry under Articles 144-145 of the Code of Criminal Procedure of the Russian Federation.
The applicant challenged the prosecutor's office decision of 28 June 2007 before a court under the procedure set out in Article 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure of the Russian Federation.
The applicant requested that the prosecutor's office decision dispensing with criminal proceedings be declared unlawful.
The applicant requested that the prosecutor's office be ordered to remedy the shortcomings in the decision dispensing with criminal proceedings.
On 20 July 2007, the Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow examined and rejected the applicant's appeal against the prosecutor's office decision of 28 June 2007.
The Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow noted that the applicant had complained to the prosecutor's office about his five-hour detention at Sheremetyevo airport.
The Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow noted that the applicant had complained to the prosecutor's office about the seizure of his ticket to Samara.

The Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow observed that the applicant had challenged the prosecutor's refusal to open criminal proceedings claiming, inter alia, that the police had unlawfully restricted his liberty.

The Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow observed that the applicant had challenged the prosecutor's refusal to open criminal proceedings claiming that the police had acted in violation of his right to freedom of expression.

The Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow observed that the applicant had challenged the prosecutor's refusal to open criminal proceedings claiming that the police had acted in violation of his right to freedom of assembly.
The Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow noted that the applicant had claimed that he had been deprived of his constitutional rights by the prosecutor's office.

The Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow considered that the prosecutor's office had taken its decision in accordance with the procedure provided for by law and remained within its competence while doing so.
The Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow upheld the finding that no criminal offence could be imputed to the police officers in question.
The Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow found the applicant's allegations about the unlawfulness of the ticket seizure to be unsubstantiated.
The Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow found that the seizure of the applicant's ticket had been carried out in accordance with Articles 27.7 and 27.10 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow found that the applicant had been taken to the airport police quarters to provide an explanation for the purchase of his ticket.
The Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow found that the applicant had not been 'isolated' at the police station at Sheremetyevo airport.

The Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow found that there had been no grounds for applying the three-hour time-limit for the application of preventative measures in administrative offences cases as provided for by the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow found that there had been no grounds for the drawing up of a detention report (протокол о задержании).
The Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow concluded that the prosecutor's decision of 28 June 2007 was lawful and well-founded.
The applicant brought a cassation appeal against the Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow's decision of 20 July 2007.
In his cassation appeal, the applicant claimed that the measures applied to him were contrary to the Code of Administrative Offences.
In his cassation appeal, the applicant claimed that there had been violations of his constitutional rights to liberty, freedom of expression and freedom of assembly.
On 20 August 2007, the Moscow City Court examined and dismissed the applicant's cassation appeal.

The Moscow City Court noted that the subject matter of the applicant's appeal to court had been the lawfulness of the prosecutor's refusal to institute criminal proceedings against the officers who had allegedly violated his constitutional rights.
The Moscow City Court upheld the decision not to institute criminal proceedings as correct in substance and form.
The Moscow City Court held that the alleged breach by the police officers of statutory detention limits were outside the scope of the Golovinskiy District Court of Moscow's power of review.
